name: Bankability Standard
description: A standard for evidence-based investment due diligence. It says what a deal folder holds and what must be known.

stages.title: Lead
stages.purpose: Capture and log new investment opportunities from all sourcing channels.

stages.title: Screening
stages.purpose: Assess whether the opportunity fits the investor's mandate, sector focus, and risk appetite.

stages.title: Concept note
stages.purpose: Produce a structured summary of the opportunity for internal review and go/no-go decision.

stages.title: Due diligence
stages.purpose: Conduct comprehensive investigation across all activated workstreams to verify claims and assess risks.

stages.title: Approval
stages.purpose: Compile findings into a formal investment recommendation for the approval committee.

stages.title: Legal documentation
stages.purpose: Complete legal due diligence and draft transaction documents including conditions precedent.

stages.title: Disbursement
stages.purpose: Verify all conditions precedent are met and execute the initial disbursement.

stages.title: Monitoring
stages.purpose: Track ongoing compliance, financial performance, and covenant adherence post-investment.

stages.title: Exit
stages.purpose: Manage loan repayment, equity exit, or portfolio wind-down and capture lessons learned.

checks.question: Is beneficial ownership fully disclosed through the control chain?
checks.assumption: Party has disclosed all natural persons who ultimately own or control it
checks.ask: Has your company fully disclosed its beneficial ownership — that is, identified all natural persons who ultimately own or control the company, directly or indirectly? We need the ownership chain traced through any intermediary companies, trusts, or other structures.
checks.if_unknown: Beneficial ownership disclosure incomplete or not provided

checks.question: Are all UBOs with more than 25% ownership identified?
checks.assumption: All significant beneficial owners (>25% threshold) are known
checks.ask: Can you confirm that every person who owns more than 25% of the company (directly or indirectly) has been identified by name, nationality, and date of birth? The 25% threshold is the standard for most AML regulations.

checks.question: Are any UBOs politically exposed persons?
checks.assumption: No beneficial owners hold or have held prominent public positions
checks.ask: Are any of the beneficial owners politically exposed persons (PEPs)? A PEP is someone who holds or has recently held a prominent public function — such as a head of state, senior government official, senior military officer, or senior judicial figure — or their close family members and associates.

leads_to.reason: UBO identified as PEP — enhanced due diligence required

checks.question: Is the beneficial ownership/control chain consistent with business rationale?
checks.assumption: Ownership structure serves a legitimate business purpose
checks.ask: Does the ownership and control chain make sense given the nature of the business? For example, is there a clear commercial reason for any holding companies, trusts, or multi-layered structures? Chains that appear more complex than the business requires can be a concern.

checks.question: Are there nominees or trust structures in the ownership chain?
checks.assumption: Ownership is held directly without nominees or trust intermediaries
checks.ask: Are any shares held by nominee shareholders or through trust structures? If so, please identify the nominee or trustee and the person on whose behalf the shares are held. We need to see through any nominee arrangements to the real beneficial owner.
checks.if_unknown: Nominee or trust arrangements not disclosed or not verifiable

why_it_matters.debt: Jurisdictional risk can affect enforceability, transferability, and sanctions exposure.
why_it_matters.equity: Country context is needed to calibrate the remaining diligence scope.

checks.question: What is the primary jurisdiction for this transaction?
checks.ask: Which country is the main jurisdiction for the borrower, investee, or principal transaction assets?
checks.if_unknown: Primary transaction jurisdiction is unknown

why_it_matters.debt: KYC/AML failures can result in regulatory action or forced exit
why_it_matters.equity: Clean compliance record supports institutional investor appetite

matters_more_when.reason: Equity thesis — reputational exposure from association with investee is higher
Equity position — reputational risk from governance association
Financial institutions face heightened AML scrutiny

checks.question: Does the entity have a compliance officer or designated compliance function?
checks.assumption: Entity has a functioning compliance oversight mechanism
checks.ask: Does your company have a compliance officer or a team responsible for regulatory compliance? This could be a dedicated compliance department or a senior person with compliance as part of their responsibilities.

checks.question: Does the entity maintain KYC records for its own clients or counterparties?
checks.assumption: Entity conducts adequate know-your-customer due diligence
checks.ask: Does your company collect and verify identity documents from your clients or business partners before entering into business relationships? This is sometimes called KYC (Know Your Customer) or CDD (Customer Due Diligence).

checks.question: Has the entity been subject to sanctions, fines, or regulatory enforcement actions?
checks.assumption: Entity has a clean regulatory record
checks.ask: Has your company ever been fined, sanctioned, or subject to enforcement action by any regulatory authority? This includes tax authorities, central banks, securities regulators, or anti-money laundering bodies. Please include any ongoing investigations.
checks.if_unknown: Sanctions/regulatory history not disclosed or not verifiable

checks.question: Does the entity have a documented AML policy?
checks.assumption: Entity has adequate anti-money laundering controls
checks.ask: Does your company have a written Anti-Money Laundering (AML) policy? This is a document that describes how the company prevents, detects, and reports suspicious financial activities. A copy of the policy would be helpful.

checks.question: What remediation steps were taken following regulatory actions or compliance gaps?
checks.assumption: Entity has addressed identified compliance deficiencies
checks.ask: If your company has faced any regulatory actions or identified compliance gaps, what steps have been taken to address them? Please describe any remediation plans, policy changes, or new controls put in place.

checks.question: Are any connected persons politically exposed persons?
checks.assumption: No directors, shareholders, or key management are PEPs
checks.ask: Are any of the company's directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, or senior managers politically exposed persons (PEPs)? A PEP is someone who holds or has recently held a prominent public function, or a close family member or associate of such a person.

checks.question: What is the nature of the PEP connection?
checks.assumption: PEP connection type is known and categorized
checks.ask: What is the nature of the PEP connection? Is the person themselves a PEP (direct), a close family member of a PEP (family), or a known close associate of a PEP (close_associate)? Please specify which individual and their relationship to the company.

checks.question: Is there enhanced due diligence documentation for the PEP?
checks.assumption: Enhanced due diligence has been performed on PEP connections
checks.ask: Has enhanced due diligence (EDD) been performed for the PEP connection? EDD typically includes verification of the source of wealth, source of funds, closer scrutiny of the business relationship, and senior management approval. Please provide any EDD documentation.

checks.question: Is there ongoing monitoring of PEP status?
checks.assumption: PEP status is monitored on an ongoing basis for changes
checks.ask: Does your company have a process for ongoing monitoring of PEP connections? This means regularly re-screening PEPs for changes in status (e.g., leaving office) and reviewing the business relationship at defined intervals. How often is PEP status reviewed?

why_it_matters.debt: Sanctions violation is a hard stop regardless of thesis frame
why_it_matters.equity: Sanctions violation is a hard stop regardless of thesis frame

checks.question: Has a sanctions screening been performed?
checks.assumption: Entity has been screened against sanctions lists
checks.ask: Has a sanctions screening been performed on your company, its directors, and its beneficial owners? This means checking names against international sanctions lists (UN, EU, OFAC, UK). If a screening has been done, please share the screening report or certificate.
checks.if_unknown: Sanctions screening not performed or results not available

checks.question: Are any entities or persons on sanctions lists?
checks.assumption: No connected parties appear on any sanctions list
checks.ask: Did the sanctions screening identify any matches — either exact or potential — against any sanctions list for the company, its directors, shareholders, or beneficial owners?
checks.if_unknown: Sanctions match status unresolved — potential matches not cleared
checks.note: If no: the topic stays relevant for monitoring.

checks.question: Are there transactions involving sanctioned jurisdictions?
checks.assumption: Entity has no business activity in or with sanctioned jurisdictions
checks.ask: Does your company conduct any business with or in jurisdictions that are subject to international sanctions? This includes selling to, buying from, or transiting goods through countries like North Korea, Iran, Syria, Cuba, or Crimea, among others.
checks.if_unknown: Geographic exposure to sanctioned jurisdictions not assessed

checks.question: Is there a sanctions compliance policy?
checks.assumption: Entity has a framework to prevent sanctions violations on an ongoing basis
checks.ask: Does your company have a written sanctions compliance policy — a document that describes how the company screens counterparties, monitors for sanctions changes, and ensures it does not engage in prohibited transactions?

checks.question: Is the source of funds for the transaction identified?
checks.assumption: The origin of funds being used in this transaction is known
checks.ask: Can you identify the source of funds for this transaction — that is, where the money is coming from? This could be operating cash flows, proceeds from a prior investment, loan proceeds, shareholder contributions, or other sources. A written declaration or bank statements showing the fund origin would be helpful.
checks.if_unknown: Source of funds not identified — critical for AML compliance

checks.question: Is the source of funds consistent with known business activities?
checks.assumption: Funds originate from the entity's normal course of business
checks.ask: Is the source of funds consistent with what we know about the company's business activities and financial position? For example, if the company claims funds come from operating profits, do the financial statements support that level of cash generation?

checks.question: Are there any unusual or complex fund flows?
checks.assumption: Fund flows follow straightforward, expected patterns
checks.ask: Are there any unusual patterns in how funds are flowing into or through the transaction? Examples of concerns include funds passing through multiple intermediary accounts without clear business reason, round-trip transactions, payments to or from unrelated third parties, or fund flows through high-risk jurisdictions.
checks.if_unknown: Fund flow patterns not assessed — bank statements or flow diagrams needed

checks.question: Is there documentation supporting the source of funds?
checks.assumption: Source of funds is evidenced by verifiable documentation
checks.ask: Can you provide documentary evidence supporting the declared source of funds? Acceptable documents include bank statements showing the fund origin, audited accounts demonstrating cash generation, loan agreements for borrowed funds, or share sale agreements for proceeds from equity disposals.

why_it_matters.debt: Primary financed-party structure determines recourse and ring-fencing effectiveness
why_it_matters.equity: Primary financed-party structure affects governance and value extraction paths

checks.question: What is the primary financed-party structure?
checks.ask: What type of entity is the primary financed party, borrower, or investee? - SPV: a special purpose vehicle set up specifically for this asset or transaction - Operating entity: a company that runs its own business with employees and operations - Holding company: a parent entity that owns subsidiaries - Fund vehicle: an investment fund (LP, SICAV, etc.)

checks.question: Does the primary financed party have employees?
checks.ask: Does this entity directly employ staff? Or is it a shell/SPV where operations are outsourced to a manager or service provider?

checks.question: Is the primary financed party part of a larger group?
checks.ask: Is this entity part of a larger corporate group? Does it have a parent company, sister companies, or other related entities?
checks.if_unknown: Group structure unknown — scope of analysis may be incomplete

leads_to.reason: Group membership increases related party transaction risk

checks.question: What is the collateral scope?
checks.ask: What is being offered or expected as collateral/security? - Single asset: one specific asset (e.g., one building, one project) - Multi-asset: a portfolio of assets - Enterprise: the whole business / all assets - Unsecured: no specific collateral

checks.question: Which entities, projects, assets, facilities, and material contracts are in the proposed transaction perimeter?
checks.ask: Please provide the transaction structure at a high level: financed-party entities, projects/assets, facilities or tranches, key contracts, and which parties are inside the transaction perimeter. A structure chart, term sheet, or short written description is enough at this stage.
checks.if_unknown: Transaction topology unknown — subject-specific diligence cannot be prioritized reliably

checks.question: Are there guarantees, support undertakings, cash sweeps, or other support links between transaction parties?
checks.ask: Are any parties supporting each other through guarantees, completion undertakings, cash sweeps, reserve sharing, cross-defaults, or other debt-service support arrangements? If yes, please identify who supports whom and when that support starts or ends.
checks.if_unknown: Support topology unknown — transaction recourse may be incomplete

leads_to.reason: Inter-party support can centralize credit risk and drive prioritization
Guarantees and undertakings need event-based trigger/release analysis

checks.question: Which events trigger or release the support arrangements?
checks.ask: For each support arrangement, what events trigger support and what events release it? Examples include project completion, financial completion, COD, DSRA funding, debt-service shortfall, facility repayment, or another documented milestone.

checks.question: Which material contracts generate or protect repayment cash flows?
checks.ask: Which contracts are most important to repayment? Please identify key offtake, concession, EPC, O&M, grid connection, supply, or management contracts and the relevant counterparties.

leads_to.reason: Contracted repayment cash flow requires counterparty credit assessment

checks.question: What is the primary cash flow basis?
checks.ask: How is the entity's cash flow primarily supported? - Contracted: long-term contracts, leases, or offtake agreements - Projected: based on forecasts and business plans (limited track record) - Historical: well-established track record of actual cash flows - Mixed: combination of contracted and market-based revenue

why_it_matters.debt: ESG failures can create covenant/regulatory risk for debt holders
why_it_matters.equity: ESG credentials affect exit universe and valuation multiples

checks.question: Is there a specific sustainability mandate or commitment?
checks.ask: Does the investor (or target investor base) have specific ESG/sustainability requirements? For example: - No specific mandate beyond basic screening - ESG integration (considering ESG factors in analysis) - SFDR Article 8 (promoting environmental/social characteristics) - SFDR Article 9 (sustainable investment objective) - DFI/impact mandate (development impact requirements) - Labelled instrument (green bond, social bond framework)

checks.question: Are there multiple investor types being targeted with different mandates?
checks.ask: Is the entity targeting multiple types of investors who may have different ESG/sustainability requirements? For example, approaching both commercial banks and impact investors, or both Article 8 and Article 9 funds?

checks.question: Are there specific exclusion lists applicable?
checks.ask: Are there specific exclusion lists that apply? For example, restrictions on fossil fuels, weapons, tobacco, controversial sectors, or specific country exclusions?

checks.question: What is the investor's position in the capital structure?
checks.ask: What type of capital is being provided or raised? Senior debt (secured or unsecured), junior/mezzanine debt, preferred or common equity, co-investment, or a guarantee?
checks.if_unknown: Capital structure position unknown — thesis frame cannot be set

checks.question: Is there an existing capital structure (other layers of financing)?
checks.ask: Does the entity already have other financing in place (existing loans, bonds, equity investors)? We need to understand how the new capital fits alongside existing commitments.

checks.question: What is the full capital structure?
checks.ask: Can you provide details of the full capital structure? This includes all existing debt facilities (amounts, seniority, maturity, lender), equity contributions, and any shareholder loans. A capitalization table or summary is ideal.
checks.if_unknown: Full capital structure not available — intercreditor and structural analysis limited

checks.question: Are multiple capital structure positions being targeted?
checks.ask: Is the entity raising capital across multiple layers of the structure simultaneously? For example, raising both senior debt and equity, or senior and mezzanine tranches?

why_it_matters.debt: Lifecycle stage determines which downside scenarios are plausible
why_it_matters.equity: Lifecycle stage determines value creation runway

checks.question: What stage is the asset or entity in?
checks.ask: What stage is this asset or entity in? - Greenfield: new build, not yet operational - Brownfield: existing site being redeveloped - Transitional: operational but undergoing significant change (renovation, repositioning, expansion) - Stabilized: fully operational with established track record - Distressed: facing financial or operational difficulties

checks.question: Is there a material capex program planned (>15% of asset value)?
checks.ask: Is there a significant capital expenditure program planned? By significant we mean more than 15% of the current asset value. This includes major renovations, expansions, equipment replacements, or new construction.

checks.question: Is there active construction or renovation?
Are projections based on current or future state?

why_it_matters.debt: Sector determines which downside risks are structural
why_it_matters.equity: Sector determines growth characteristics and exit universe

checks.question: What is the primary business activity of the entity?
checks.ask: What does this entity primarily do? Own/manage properties, build/operate infrastructure, manufacture/sell goods or services, provide financial services, manage investments?

checks.question: What is the specific sector or property type?
checks.ask: What specific type of asset does this entity focus on? For example: office, logistics, residential, renewable energy, transport, manufacturing, etc.

checks.question: Is the entity a regulated financial institution?
checks.ask: Is this entity regulated as a financial institution (bank, insurer, fund manager, broker-dealer)?
checks.if_unknown: Regulatory status unknown — may affect scope of analysis

checks.question: Where does the entity sit in its sector's value chain?
checks.ask: What is the entity's primary role? E.g., does it develop assets, own and manage them, provide services, manufacture goods, or manage investments?

checks.question: Does the entity own or lease physical property as a primary activity?
Is revenue primarily from rent, lease payments, or property sales?

why_it_matters.debt: Environmental liabilities can be material and difficult to quantify
why_it_matters.equity: Strong environmental credentials command green premium and wider investor universe

matters_more_when.reason: DFI mandate — environmental safeguards and impact measurement essential
Greenfield — environmental impact assessment is typically a regulatory requirement
Infrastructure projects typically require environmental permits

matters_less_when.reason: No ESG mandate — environmental analysis limited to regulatory compliance

checks.question: Has an environmental impact assessment been conducted?
checks.assumption: Environmental impact has been formally assessed
checks.ask: Has an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) or Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) been conducted? A copy of the report, the EIA certificate, or the environmental permit would be ideal.
checks.if_unknown: Environmental impact status unknown — regulatory and liability risk

checks.question: Are there identified environmental liabilities or contamination issues?
checks.assumption: No material environmental liabilities exist
checks.ask: Are there any known environmental liabilities, contamination issues, or remediation obligations? This includes soil or water contamination, hazardous waste, or environmental provisions in your accounts.
checks.if_unknown: Environmental liability status not confirmed — potential hidden exposure

checks.question: Does the entity comply with local environmental regulations and hold required permits?
checks.assumption: Entity is in compliance with environmental regulations
checks.ask: Does your entity hold all required environmental permits and comply with local environmental regulations? Please share copies of permits, compliance certificates, or confirmation of regulatory status.

checks.question: Are there GHG emission reporting requirements applicable to the entity?
checks.assumption: Entity has no GHG reporting obligations
checks.ask: Is your entity required to report greenhouse gas emissions — either by regulation or voluntary commitment? If you produce a sustainability report or carbon disclosure, please share it.

checks.question: Has a climate risk assessment been conducted covering physical and transition risks?
checks.assumption: Climate risks have been formally assessed
checks.ask: Has your entity conducted a climate risk assessment? This could cover physical risks (flooding, drought, extreme weather) and transition risks (regulatory changes, carbon pricing, technology shifts). A TCFD disclosure or scenario analysis would be ideal.
checks.if_unknown: Climate risk exposure not assessed — emerging regulatory and physical risk

checks.question: Does the entity comply with applicable labor laws and employment standards?
checks.assumption: Entity is in compliance with labor laws
checks.ask: Does your entity comply with local labor laws and employment standards? This includes employment contracts, minimum wage, working hours, and occupational health and safety. HR policies, labor inspection reports, or a brief confirmation would be helpful.

checks.question: Are there community impact concerns related to the entity's operations?
checks.assumption: No material community impact concerns exist
checks.ask: Are there any community impact concerns related to your operations? This could include land acquisition, resettlement, noise, traffic, or effects on local livelihoods. Stakeholder consultation records or the social chapter of an ESIA would be relevant.
checks.if_unknown: Community impact not assessed — social licence risk

checks.question: Is there a grievance mechanism accessible to workers and affected communities?
checks.assumption: A functional grievance mechanism is in place
checks.ask: Does your entity have a grievance mechanism for workers and affected communities? This could be a formal complaints procedure, whistleblower hotline, or community feedback mechanism. A description of the process or a copy of the policy would help.

checks.question: Has there been any labor dispute, workplace incident, or regulatory action in the last 3 years?
checks.assumption: No labor disputes or workplace incidents in the last 3 years
checks.ask: Have there been any labor disputes, significant workplace incidents, or regulatory actions (fines, inspections, enforcement) in the last 3 years? Please disclose any strikes, tribunal cases, workplace injuries, or labor authority findings.
checks.if_unknown: Labor dispute and incident history not disclosed

checks.question: Does this guarantee or undertaking support project completion or performance?
checks.why: Completion support can be a core mitigant for construction-phase project finance
checks.ask: Does this guarantee or support undertaking cover project completion, commissioning, performance tests, or cost-to-complete obligations?

checks.question: What event triggers the completion support?
checks.why: Trigger events determine when support is actually available

checks.question: What event releases the completion support?
checks.why: Release events define how long the support remains available

checks.question: What evidence is required to prove the release event?
checks.why: Release should depend on objective evidence rather than an unsupported assertion

checks.question: Is the completion support enforceable and capped at an adequate level?
checks.why: Weak enforceability or a low cap can make completion support ineffective

why_it_matters.debt: Cost escalation or fixed-cost inflexibility can erode debt service capacity
why_it_matters.equity: Cost optimization potential affects margin expansion and value creation

matters_more_when.reason: Manufacturer — cost structure is the primary margin driver
Contractor — input costs and labor drive profitability
Projected cashflow — cost assumptions need validation
Stabilized — cost history provides reliable baseline for projections

matters_less_when.reason: SPV — limited cost base, operating costs typically pass-through

checks.question: What is the gross margin?
checks.assumption: Core business is profitable at the unit level
checks.ask: What is your company's gross margin (gross profit as a percentage of revenue)? If you don't have this calculated, we can work it out from your revenue and cost of goods sold figures.

checks.question: Is the cost structure primarily fixed or variable?
checks.assumption: Cost structure provides operational flexibility
checks.ask: Would you say most of your costs are fixed (rent, salaries, insurance) or variable (raw materials, commissions, shipping)? Or is it roughly balanced between the two?

checks.question: Are there significant input cost dependencies?
checks.assumption: Input costs are diversified and stable
checks.ask: Is your company heavily dependent on any single input cost — for example, a specific raw material, commodity, or energy source that makes up a large share of your total costs?
checks.if_unknown: Input cost dependency unknown — supply and margin risk may be understated

checks.question: Has the entity experienced margin compression in the last 2 years?
checks.assumption: Margins have been stable or improving
checks.ask: Have your profit margins decreased over the past 2 years? For example, has gross margin or operating margin fallen compared to previous years?
checks.if_unknown: Historical margin trend not available

checks.question: Are there material related-party costs?
checks.assumption: All costs are transacted with independent third parties
checks.ask: Does your company pay significant amounts to related parties — for example, management fees to a parent company, rent to a shareholder-owned property, or purchases from affiliated companies?

leads_to.reason: Material related-party costs require arm's-length verification

checks.question: What financial covenants are appropriate based on the entity's financial profile?
checks.assumption: Appropriate financial covenants have been identified for monitoring
checks.ask: Based on your company's financial profile, which financial covenants do you expect in the loan agreement? Common examples include debt service coverage ratio (DSCR), leverage ratio, current ratio, or minimum net worth. What ratios does your company currently achieve?

checks.question: Are information and reporting covenants clearly defined?
checks.assumption: Borrower reporting obligations are specified and achievable
checks.ask: What reporting and information requirements will be in the loan agreement? For example, how frequently will you need to provide financial statements, compliance certificates, and management reports? Can your finance team produce these on time?

checks.question: Are there negative pledge provisions and restrictions on additional indebtedness?
checks.assumption: Borrower's ability to incur additional debt is appropriately restricted
checks.ask: Will the loan agreement include a negative pledge (preventing you from granting security to other lenders) or restrictions on taking on additional debt? Are these restrictions workable for your business plans?

checks.question: Are financial covenant levels set with appropriate headroom above current performance?
checks.assumption: Covenant levels provide a meaningful early warning without being too tight
checks.ask: Are the proposed covenant levels realistic? For example, if a DSCR covenant is set at 1.2x, does your company currently achieve at least 1.5x to provide a reasonable cushion? Have you tested covenant levels under downside scenarios?

checks.question: Are cure rights and remedy provisions defined for covenant breaches?
checks.assumption: Clear remediation process exists if covenants are breached
checks.ask: If a financial covenant is breached, what happens? Is there a cure period (time to fix the breach)? Can the sponsor inject equity to cure? What are the lender's remedies — waiver, acceleration, or other consequences?

why_it_matters.debt: Debt burden and maturity profile are the primary downside concern for lenders
why_it_matters.hybrid: Mezzanine/subordinated position requires understanding of senior debt cushion
why_it_matters.equity: Debt is relevant context for equity but not the primary value driver

matters_more_when.reason: Senior secured investor — understanding existing debt structure is critical
Senior unsecured investor — debt layering and subordination matter
Existing capital structure — intercreditor dynamics need assessment
Distressed entity — debt restructuring analysis essential

matters_less_when.reason: Equity investor — debt is context, not the primary concern

checks.question: Does the entity have existing debt?
checks.assumption: Entity is debt-free
checks.ask: Does your company currently owe money to any banks, lenders, or other creditors? A simple yes or no is enough to start — we can get into the details later.

checks.question: What is the total debt outstanding?
checks.assumption: Debt quantum is immaterial
checks.ask: What is the total amount of debt your company currently owes across all lenders? Please include both short-term and long-term borrowings. An approximate figure from your latest accounts is fine.
checks.if_unknown: Total debt figure not available in current documents

checks.question: What is the debt maturity profile?
checks.assumption: Debt maturity is well-distributed
checks.ask: Is most of your debt due within the next year (short-term), spread across different timeframes (balanced), or mostly due in more than a year (long-term)? You can share a maturity schedule if available.

checks.question: Is there subordinated or mezzanine debt in the capital structure?
checks.assumption: All debt is senior / pari passu
checks.ask: Does your company have any subordinated debt or mezzanine financing? This is debt that ranks below senior lenders in priority of repayment.

checks.question: Are there debt covenants in existing facilities?
checks.assumption: Existing debt is covenant-free
checks.ask: Do your current loan agreements include financial covenants — for example, minimum debt service coverage, maximum leverage, or restrictions on additional borrowing?

leads_to.reason: Existing covenants need review for new facility structuring

checks.question: What is the current debt-to-equity ratio?
checks.assumption: Leverage is within acceptable range
checks.ask: What is your company's debt-to-equity ratio? If you don't have this calculated, we can work it out from your latest balance sheet — just share total debt and total equity figures.

checks.question: What is the capital adequacy ratio (CAR) and tier 1 ratio?
checks.assumption: Institution is adequately capitalized
checks.ask: What is your current capital adequacy ratio (CAR) and tier 1 capital ratio? Please provide the most recent figures — ideally from your latest prudential return or audited financial statements.

checks.question: What is the regulatory minimum CAR and how much buffer exists?
checks.assumption: Capital buffer above regulatory minimum is adequate
checks.ask: What is the regulatory minimum capital adequacy ratio required by your central bank or regulator? How much buffer does your current CAR provide above this minimum? Has this buffer been narrowing or widening over the past 3 years?

checks.question: What is the institution's dividend policy relative to capital needs?
checks.assumption: Dividend policy supports capital retention and growth
checks.ask: What is your institution's dividend policy? What percentage of profits has been distributed as dividends over the past 3 years? Is there a formal policy that links dividend payments to capital adequacy levels?

checks.question: Does the institution have subordinated debt counting as tier 2 capital?
checks.assumption: Capital structure includes subordinated debt for regulatory capital
checks.ask: Does your institution have any subordinated debt that qualifies as tier 2 regulatory capital? If so, what are the amounts, maturity dates, and terms? Are any of these instruments approaching maturity or callable?

checks.question: Is the planned growth trajectory sustainable given current capital?
checks.assumption: Growth plans can be funded without breaching capital requirements
checks.ask: What is your planned loan book growth rate for the next 2-3 years? Have you modeled whether your current capital base — plus expected retained earnings — can support this growth without falling below regulatory minimums? A capital plan or projection would be ideal.
checks.if_unknown: Capital adequacy projections not available

checks.question: What is the institution's current central bank supervision status?
checks.assumption: Institution is in good standing with the regulator
checks.ask: What is your institution's current supervisory status with the central bank or primary regulator? Is it normal supervision, or is the institution under any enhanced monitoring, corrective action plan, or other special regulatory measures?

checks.question: Are there any material regulatory compliance findings in the past 3 years?
checks.assumption: Institution has a clean regulatory compliance history
checks.ask: Has your institution received any material findings, sanctions, penalties, or directives from the central bank or other regulators in the past 3 years? If so, please describe the nature of the findings and what remedial actions have been taken.

checks.question: Does the institution engage in related party lending?
checks.assumption: No material insider or related party lending exists
checks.ask: Does your institution have any loans or credit facilities extended to directors, shareholders, management, or their related entities? If so, what is the total exposure as a percentage of capital, and are these within regulatory single-borrower and insider lending limits?

leads_to.reason: Related party lending detected — requires dedicated related party assessment

checks.question: Does the institution have a functioning risk committee?
checks.assumption: Board-level risk oversight is formally established
checks.ask: Does your institution have a dedicated risk management committee at the board level? How often does it meet, and does it have a formal charter or terms of reference? Please share the committee charter or recent meeting minutes if available.

checks.question: Is the institution subject to independent external audit?
checks.assumption: Financial statements are independently verified
checks.ask: Are your financial statements audited by an independent external auditor? Who is your current auditor, and have there been any auditor changes in the past 3 years? Were there any qualified opinions or emphasis-of-matter paragraphs in recent audit reports?

checks.question: What is the liquid assets ratio?
checks.assumption: Institution holds adequate liquid assets relative to liabilities
checks.ask: What is your current liquid assets ratio — i.e., liquid assets (cash, government securities, central bank balances) as a percentage of total deposits or short-term liabilities? The latest prudential return figure would be ideal.

checks.question: Is the deposit base concentrated in a small number of depositors?
checks.assumption: Deposit base is diversified and stable
checks.ask: Do your top 10 or top 20 depositors account for a significant share of total deposits — for example, more than 25%? A deposit concentration analysis showing the breakdown by depositor size bands would be very helpful.

checks.question: Is there a material maturity mismatch between assets and liabilities?
checks.assumption: Asset and liability maturities are reasonably matched
checks.ask: Does your institution have a significant maturity mismatch — for example, funding long-term loans with short-term deposits? Please share your asset-liability maturity ladder or gap analysis if available.

checks.question: Does the institution have access to central bank or lender-of-last-resort facilities?
checks.assumption: Emergency liquidity backstop is available
checks.ask: Does your institution have access to central bank lending facilities — such as a discount window, repo facility, or emergency lending arrangements? Has the institution used these facilities in the past 12 months?

checks.question: What is the institution's interbank exposure?
checks.assumption: Interbank exposure is manageable and well-monitored
checks.ask: What is the size of your interbank placements and borrowings — both as absolute amounts and as a percentage of total assets? Are these primarily overnight, short-term, or longer-term? Has interbank exposure been increasing or decreasing?
checks.if_unknown: Interbank exposure data not available

checks.question: What is the non-performing loan (NPL) ratio?
checks.assumption: Asset quality is within acceptable bounds
checks.ask: What is your current non-performing loan (NPL) ratio — i.e., the percentage of your total loan portfolio that is classified as non-performing (typically 90+ days past due)? The latest prudential return or audited financials would be ideal.

checks.question: Is the provisioning level adequate relative to NPLs?
checks.assumption: Loan loss provisions adequately cover non-performing exposures
checks.ask: What is your provision coverage ratio — i.e., total loan loss provisions as a percentage of non-performing loans? A ratio above 100% indicates full coverage. Please share the breakdown by loan classification category if available.

checks.question: Is the loan portfolio concentrated by sector, geography, or single borrower?
checks.assumption: Portfolio is diversified across sectors, geographies, and borrowers
checks.ask: Is your loan portfolio concentrated in any single sector (e.g., agriculture, real estate), geographic region, or individual borrower? Specifically, does any single sector exceed 25% of the portfolio, or any single borrower exceed 10%? Portfolio segmentation data would be very helpful.

checks.question: What is the volume and trend of restructured loans?
checks.assumption: Restructured loans are not masking underlying asset quality deterioration
checks.ask: What percentage of your loan portfolio has been restructured in the past 12 months? Has this percentage been increasing or decreasing over time? Please include the criteria you use for classifying a loan as restructured.
checks.if_unknown: Restructured loan data not available

checks.question: Does the entity have a documented write-off policy?
checks.assumption: Write-off practices follow a formal, documented policy
checks.ask: Does your institution have a formal, documented policy for writing off non-performing loans? What are the criteria and approval thresholds? Please share a copy of the write-off policy or the relevant section of your credit policy manual.

why_it_matters.debt: Unhedged FX exposure can create cash flow volatility affecting debt service
why_it_matters.equity: FX exposure is a risk factor, not a value driver for equity

matters_more_when.reason: Corporate entities more likely to have cross-border revenue/cost mismatches
Primary producers often sell in USD but incur costs in local currency
Manufacturers may have imported input costs creating natural FX exposure

risk.statement: This party has material currency mismatch or convertibility exposure

mitigant.statement: FX exposure is adequately mitigated through hedging or natural offsets

look_again_when.reason: New hedging documentation filed — re-evaluate mitigation adequacy
Revenue geographic mix changed — FX exposure may have shifted
FX percentage and hedge coverage data older than 6 months

checks.question: Does the entity have material foreign currency revenue?
checks.assumption: Entity has no FX exposure
checks.ask: Does your company earn revenue in foreign currencies? You can answer with a revenue breakdown by currency, your latest annual report, or simply tell us the approximate share.
checks.note: If no: confirm cost, debt-service, translation, capex and convertibility exposure before treating currency risk as closed.

checks.question: What percentage of revenue is in foreign currency?
checks.assumption: FX revenue is immaterial
checks.ask: What share of your revenue comes from foreign currencies? A rough percentage is fine at this stage.

checks.question: In which currencies does the entity earn revenue?
checks.assumption: FX exposure is in stable currencies only

checks.question: Does the entity have any foreign-currency-denominated costs?
checks.assumption: Entity has zero FX exposure
checks.if_unknown: Cost currency breakdown not available in current documents

checks.question: Is debt service or borrowing denominated in a currency different from the entity's operating cash flows?
checks.assumption: Debt service currency is naturally matched to operating cash flows
checks.ask: Is any borrowing or debt service in a different currency from the cash flows used to repay it? For example, USD or EUR debt serviced from local-currency revenue.

checks.question: What share of input costs is imported or priced on import parity (FX-linked)?
checks.assumption: Input costs are local-currency with no import linkage
checks.ask: Roughly what share of your input costs is imported, or priced off international markets in hard currency even when billed locally (for example imported gas, fuels, or raw materials)? Raw materials in transit and import letters of credit in your accounts are useful reference points.

checks.question: Can FX-driven input cost increases be passed through to selling prices within one quarter?
checks.assumption: Pricing freedom absorbs FX-driven cost shocks
checks.ask: When a weaker currency raises your input costs, can you raise selling prices to match within a quarter — fully, partly, or are your prices administered or capped by policy?

checks.question: Are material assets, liabilities, or earnings translated from foreign currencies?
checks.assumption: Foreign-currency translation exposure is immaterial
checks.ask: Do you have material assets, liabilities, subsidiaries, or earnings that are reported in a different currency and translated into your reporting currency?

checks.question: Are material capex or procurement commitments denominated in foreign currency?
checks.assumption: Capital expenditure and procurement are naturally currency-matched
checks.ask: Are any major capex, equipment, or procurement commitments priced in a foreign currency?

checks.question: Could capital controls or convertibility restrictions affect debt service or cash movement?
checks.assumption: Cash can be converted and transferred without material restriction
checks.ask: Are there any capital controls, convertibility limits, or transfer restrictions that could affect cash movement or debt service?

checks.question: Does the entity have a formal FX hedging policy or documented FX hedge programme?
checks.assumption: Entity manages FX risk through documented policy or hedge programme
checks.ask: Does your company have a written policy or documented hedge programme for managing foreign exchange risk? This could be a treasury policy, risk management framework, board-approved hedging guidelines, or documented hedge confirmations.

checks.question: What hedging instruments are used?
checks.assumption: Entity uses appropriate hedging instruments for its risk profile
checks.ask: What types of hedging instruments does your company use to manage foreign exchange risk? Common examples include forward contracts, options, or currency swaps.

checks.question: What percentage of FX exposure is hedged?
checks.assumption: Entity has adequate hedge coverage
checks.ask: What portion of your foreign currency exposure is currently hedged? An approximate percentage is fine.
checks.note: This is the company's own statement of adequacy. Look for independent support.

checks.question: Is there a natural FX offset from costs in the same currency?
checks.assumption: Unhedged FX exposure is truly unmitigated
checks.ask: Even without a formal hedging policy, does your company have significant costs in the same foreign currencies as your revenue? This natural offset can reduce risk without formal hedging.

checks.question: Does hedge tenor cover the relevant exposure or debt-service period?
checks.assumption: Hedges mature before the relevant exposure period
checks.ask: Do the hedges cover the same period as the underlying foreign-currency exposure or debt-service period?

checks.question: Are hedge counterparties creditworthy and documented under enforceable agreements?
checks.why: Hedge counterparty or documentation risk can undermine mitigation
checks.ask: Are the hedge counterparties acceptable credit institutions, and are the hedge agreements properly documented?

why_it_matters.debt: An input interruption stops production and debt service capacity directly
why_it_matters.equity: Secured cheap input supply can be a structural margin advantage

matters_more_when.reason: Primary producers typically convert one feedstock; concentration is structural
Manufacturers often depend on a small number of critical inputs or utilities

risk.statement: Production depends on a concentrated or interruptible critical input

mitigant.statement: Input supply is secured by tenor, price protection, or substitutability

look_again_when.reason: Supply interruption occurred — re-evaluate severity and mitigants
New supply contract filed — re-evaluate tenor and price protection
Interruption and contract-tenor data older than 6 months

checks.question: Does any single input (commodity, utility, or supplier) account for a material share of production cost?
checks.assumption: Input base is diversified; no single dependency
checks.ask: Is there one input — a feedstock, raw material, or utility such as gas or power — that your production cannot run without, or one supplier that provides a large share of your input costs? Name the input and supplier if so.
checks.note: If no: check the answer against the composition of cost of sales before treating the topic as closed.

checks.question: What share of cost of sales does the largest single input represent?
checks.assumption: Largest input is below the concentration threshold
checks.ask: Roughly what share of your cost of sales is the single largest input (for example feedstock gas, key raw material, or energy)?

checks.question: How many qualified suppliers can deliver the critical input at the required volume?
checks.assumption: Input is freely substitutable across suppliers
checks.ask: Could another supplier deliver this input at the volume you need — or is there effectively only one source (for example a dedicated gas allocation or single pipeline)?
checks.if_unknown: Supplier substitutability unknown — single-source risk cannot be assessed

checks.question: Is the input price or allocation administered by government policy, levy, or sovereign commitment?
checks.assumption: Input pricing is market-based with no policy dependency
checks.ask: Is the price or allocation of this input set or guaranteed by government policy — for example a sovereign pricing commitment, an allocation quota, or a levy/cess regime?

checks.question: Has supply of the critical input been interrupted or curtailed in the last 24 months?
checks.assumption: No interruptions in the recent operating record
checks.ask: Has this input ever been cut, curtailed, or suspended in the last two years — even briefly? Production volume tables in your reports will be compared against capacity, so please include partial curtailments.
checks.note: The company has a reason to understate this. Check it against an independent source.

checks.question: What is the remaining tenor of the supply contract in years?
checks.assumption: Supply is contracted well beyond the financing horizon
checks.ask: Until when is the supply of this input contractually secured? Please state the end date of the current supply agreement or allocation.
checks.if_unknown: Supply contract tenor unknown — cannot compare against facility maturity

checks.question: Is there pending litigation or regulatory action affecting input price or supply (levies, cess, allocation disputes)?
checks.assumption: No input-side legal or regulatory exposure
checks.ask: Are there any court cases, levies under dispute, or regulatory proceedings that affect what you pay for this input or whether you receive it?

checks.question: Which structural protections exist for the critical input?
checks.assumption: No structural protection exists
checks.ask: What protects this supply: a fixed-price or sovereign commitment, a take-or-pay contract, storage you control, or a second source?

checks.question: Can production switch to an alternative input or alternative plant within one quarter?
checks.assumption: Substitution is not feasible within a relevant horizon
checks.ask: If this input stopped tomorrow, could you keep producing — by switching fuel, plant, or product mix — within roughly three months?

checks.question: What share of earnings is generated by operations NOT dependent on the concentrated input source?
checks.assumption: Cash generation is diversified across input sources
checks.ask: Of your operating earnings, roughly what share comes from plants or operations that do not rely on the concentrated input source?

why_it_matters.debt: Liquidity shortfall is often the proximate cause of default
why_it_matters.equity: Excess liquidity may indicate inefficient capital deployment
why_it_matters.hybrid: liquidity risk for subordinated positions — cash sweep exposure

matters_more_when.reason: Operating entity — working capital and liquidity management are core
Distressed entity — liquidity is the immediate survival concern
Greenfield — liquidity needs during construction phase are critical

matters_less_when.reason: SPV — liquidity typically governed by reserve accounts and waterfall

checks.question: Does the entity maintain cash reserves?
checks.assumption: Entity has no liquidity buffer
checks.ask: Does your company keep cash reserves or liquid investments on hand? A simple yes or no is fine — we will ask about the amount later if needed.

checks.question: What is the current ratio?
checks.assumption: Short-term liquidity is adequate
checks.ask: What is your company's current ratio (current assets divided by current liabilities)? If you don't have this number handy, we can calculate it from your latest balance sheet.

checks.question: Does the entity have access to committed credit lines?
checks.assumption: Entity has no backstop liquidity facility
checks.ask: Does your company have access to any committed credit lines or overdraft facilities that you can draw on if needed? Please include both drawn and undrawn amounts.

checks.question: Has the entity experienced cash flow shortfalls in the past 2 years?
checks.assumption: Cash flow has been consistently positive
checks.ask: In the last two years, has your company ever run short of cash to meet its obligations — for example, delayed payments to suppliers, missed payroll, or needed emergency funding?
checks.if_unknown: Cash flow history not available for the past 2 years

checks.question: What is the average days payable outstanding?
checks.assumption: Payment practices are within normal terms
checks.ask: On average, how many days does it take your company to pay its suppliers? If you have an accounts payable aging report, that would be ideal.

checks.question: Is this contract or counterparty responsible for a material share of contracted project revenue?
checks.why: Material offtakers can centralize repayment risk
checks.ask: Is this contract or counterparty expected to buy a material share of the project's output or otherwise provide contracted revenue?

checks.question: What share of project revenue depends on this offtaker?
checks.why: Revenue share drives offtaker materiality and ask depth
checks.ask: Approximately what percentage of project revenue depends on this offtaker or PPA?

checks.question: What is the offtaker or revenue counterparty's credit quality?
checks.why: Offtaker credit quality determines reliability of contracted cash flow
checks.ask: What is the offtaker or revenue counterparty's credit quality? For a government offtaker, please provide the relevant sovereign/public-sector rating or credit memo.

checks.question: Has the offtaker paid on time under comparable contracts?
checks.why: Strong ratings do not fully replace payment performance
checks.ask: Is there evidence that this offtaker pays on time under this or comparable contracts?

checks.question: Does the contract protect lenders on termination, curtailment, or non-payment?
checks.why: Termination and curtailment protections preserve debt service under stress
checks.ask: Does the offtake/PPA include protections for termination, curtailment, non-payment, and lender step-in or termination compensation?

checks.question: Is this portfolio support arrangement documented and binding?
checks.why: Support between projects only mitigates risk if it is legally documented
checks.ask: Is the cash sweep or portfolio support arrangement documented and legally binding? Please share the agreement, cash waterfall, or term sheet section that describes it.

checks.question: What type of support is provided?
checks.why: Support type determines how much risk is centralized across projects

checks.question: Is support mandatory when the trigger event occurs?
checks.why: Discretionary support is weaker than mandatory debt-service support

checks.question: Where does the support sit in the cash waterfall?
checks.why: Waterfall priority determines whether excess cash is actually available for support

checks.question: Which events trigger the support?
checks.why: Support only matters when the trigger event is clear

checks.question: Which events release or terminate the support?
checks.why: Release events determine whether support remains available through the relevant risk period

look_again_when.reason: Reporting perimeter changed — historical baselines behind projections need restatement flags
Critical input interruption occurred — stress production-linked projection assumptions

checks.question: Has the entity prepared financial projections?
checks.assumption: Entity has forward-looking financial plans
checks.ask: Has your company prepared financial projections or forecasts — for example, a financial model, business plan with projected financials, or a detailed budget? A simple yes or no is fine.

checks.question: What period do projections cover?
checks.assumption: Projection horizon is adequate for the financing tenor
checks.ask: How far into the future do your financial projections extend? Is it 1 year, 3 years, 5 years, or beyond 5 years?

checks.question: Are key assumptions documented?
checks.assumption: Projections are built on documented, testable assumptions
checks.ask: Are the key assumptions behind your projections written down — for example, revenue growth rates, cost inflation, pricing assumptions, and capital expenditure plans? This is typically an assumptions page in a financial model or an appendix in a business plan.

checks.question: Have projections been independently reviewed?
checks.assumption: Projections have been validated by an independent party
checks.ask: Have your financial projections been reviewed or audited by an independent party — for example, a model auditor, independent financial adviser, or your external auditors?

checks.question: How do projections compare to historical performance?
checks.assumption: Projections are grounded in historical performance
checks.ask: Compared to your company's actual performance over the past few years, would you describe the projections as conservative (below historical trends), in line with historical trends, or aggressive (significantly above historical trends)?

checks.question: Does the entity engage in related party transactions?
checks.assumption: Entity has no related party dealings
checks.ask: Does your company buy from, sell to, or otherwise transact with related parties — such as shareholders, directors, affiliated companies, or family members of key management?

checks.question: What is the total value of related party transactions as a percentage of revenue?
checks.assumption: Related party transactions are immaterial
checks.ask: What is the total value of all transactions with related parties, expressed as a percentage of your total revenue? The notes to your audited accounts should have this breakdown.

checks.question: Are related party transactions at arm's length?
checks.assumption: Related party transactions are conducted on commercial terms
checks.ask: Are your transactions with related parties priced at market rates — meaning on the same terms you would offer to an unrelated third party? If you have transfer pricing documentation or auditor confirmation, that would be helpful.
checks.if_unknown: Arm's-length status of related party transactions not confirmed

checks.question: Is there a related party transaction policy?
checks.assumption: Related party transactions are governed by a formal policy
checks.ask: Does your company have a formal policy for approving and monitoring related party transactions? This might be part of your corporate governance framework or board charter.

checks.question: Have related party transactions been disclosed in audited financials?
checks.assumption: Related party transactions are fully disclosed per accounting standards
checks.ask: Are all related party transactions disclosed in the notes to your audited financial statements, as required by accounting standards (IAS 24 or equivalent)?

checks.question: What is total related-party lending (loans plus receivables) as a share of tangible equity?
checks.assumption: Related-party lending is immaterial to the capital base
checks.ask: Add up all loans and receivables owed to you by related parties (group companies, associates, sponsors). What is that total as a share of your equity?

checks.question: What was the maximum related-party loan balance during the period relative to the period-end balance?
checks.assumption: The period-end balance is representative of the year
checks.ask: Your accounts may disclose the maximum amount of each related-party loan outstanding during the year. How does that peak compare to the year-end balance? A peak well above year-end means the year-end figure understates the real exposure.

checks.question: Are related-party loans repayable on demand, and could the borrower actually repay if demanded?
checks.assumption: Loans are recoverable on their stated terms
checks.ask: For loans to group companies: can you demand repayment (for example on 30 days' notice), and does the borrowing company have the liquidity to actually pay if you did? A demand right against an illiquid borrower provides little protection.
checks.if_unknown: Recoverability of related-party loans not assessed against borrower liquidity

checks.question: Has a scheme of arrangement, carve-out, or group restructuring changed the reporting perimeter in the last 24 months?
checks.assumption: The reporting perimeter is stable; period-on-period trends are comparable
checks.ask: In the last two years, has any plant, division, or subsidiary been moved into or out of the reporting entity — for example through a scheme of arrangement, carve-out, demerger, or amalgamation? If so, which periods are affected?
checks.if_unknown: Perimeter stability unknown — historical trend analysis may be misleading
checks.note: This is the company's own statement. Look for independent support.

why_it_matters.debt: Revenue stability and predictability directly affect debt service capacity
why_it_matters.equity: Revenue growth trajectory affects value creation and exit multiples

matters_more_when.reason: Contracted cashflow — revenue analysis focuses on counterparty quality and contract terms
Single asset — revenue concentration inherent, analysis is critical
Contractor value chain — project-based revenue needs pipeline analysis
Stabilized — historical revenue track record is key evidence

matters_less_when.reason: Fund vehicle — revenue analysis less relevant, NAV and portfolio analysis instead
Greenfield — no operating revenue yet, projections indicator more relevant

checks.question: Does the entity generate revenue?
checks.assumption: Entity is pre-revenue
checks.ask: Does your company currently earn revenue from selling products or services? A simple yes or no is fine.

checks.question: What is the primary revenue model?
checks.assumption: Revenue model is diversified
checks.ask: How does your company primarily earn money? Is it through selling products, providing services, subscription fees, project-based contracts, or a mix of these?

checks.question: Is revenue concentrated in fewer than 3 customers?
checks.assumption: Revenue base is diversified across customers
checks.ask: Do your top 3 customers account for more than half of your total revenue? If you can share a breakdown of revenue by customer, that would be very helpful.
checks.if_unknown: Customer concentration unknown — revenue resilience may be overstated

checks.question: What is the revenue growth rate over the last 3 years?
checks.assumption: Revenue trajectory is stable or growing
checks.ask: What has your average annual revenue growth been over the past 3 years? If you can share revenue figures for each of the last 3 years, we can calculate this.

checks.question: Is revenue seasonal?
checks.assumption: Revenue is evenly distributed throughout the year
checks.ask: Does your revenue vary significantly by season or time of year? For example, do you earn most of your revenue during certain months or quarters?

checks.question: Are there contracted or recurring revenue streams?
checks.assumption: All revenue is transactional / one-off
checks.ask: Does your company have any long-term contracts, subscriptions, or recurring revenue arrangements that provide predictable income? Examples include supply agreements, service contracts, or subscription plans.

checks.question: Does any single customer account for 10% or more of revenue (IFRS 8 major-customer disclosure)?
checks.assumption: The revenue base is granular with no major customer
checks.ask: Do the notes to your audited accounts disclose any customer that represents 10% or more of revenue? Note: under IFRS 8 auditors must disclose this — the absence of the disclosure is itself evidence of a granular customer base.

checks.question: What share of trade receivables is credit-enhanced (bank guarantees, letters of credit, collateral)?
checks.assumption: Receivables are substantially credit-enhanced
checks.ask: Of the money customers owe you, what share is covered by bank guarantees, letters of credit, or other collateral? Your trade receivables note typically splits secured from unsecured.

checks.question: What share of total receivables is due from government bodies (subsidies, tax refunds, duties)?
checks.assumption: Government receivables are immaterial
checks.ask: How much of what you are owed comes from government bodies — unpaid subsidies, tax or duty refunds, or sales to state entities — and how old are those balances?

checks.question: What share of revenue is collected in advance as customer prepayments (contract liabilities)?
checks.assumption: Customers do not prefund purchases
checks.ask: Do customers pay you before delivery? Your balance sheet may show this as contract liabilities or advances from customers. Roughly what share of a year's sales is prepaid at any time? This is a strength signal — it indicates market power and reduces collection risk.

why_it_matters.debt: Security package quality determines recovery rate in downside scenarios
why_it_matters.equity: Security package is not a value driver for equity investors
why_it_matters.hybrid: subordination analysis — priority of claims in waterfall

matters_more_when.reason: Senior secured — security package is the primary downside protection
Mezzanine — second-priority security or structural protections matter
Senior unsecured — negative pledge and structural protections may substitute

matters_less_when.reason: Equity investor — no security package; value protection through governance instead
Preferred equity — limited security; liquidation preference provides some protection

checks.question: What assets are available as security for the proposed transaction?
checks.assumption: Entity has identifiable assets available as collateral
checks.ask: What assets does your company own that could be offered as security for this financing? Examples include real estate, equipment, receivables, inventory, or shares in subsidiaries. A summary of major assets with approximate values would be helpful.

checks.question: Is a corporate guarantee available from a parent company or sponsor?
checks.assumption: Transaction has credit support beyond the borrower's own assets
checks.ask: Is a parent company, holding company, or sponsor willing to provide a corporate guarantee for this transaction? If so, please share their financial statements so we can assess the guarantee's value.

checks.question: Is real estate security available and unencumbered?
checks.assumption: Real property collateral is available and free of prior claims
checks.ask: Does the company own real estate (land or buildings) that could serve as security? Are these properties free of existing mortgages or liens? Title deeds and a recent valuation would be very helpful.

leads_to.reason: Real estate available as security — technical condition assessment needed

checks.question: Are cash flow assignments from specific contracts or revenue streams feasible?
checks.assumption: Cash flow assignment is a viable security mechanism
checks.ask: Can specific revenue streams or contract payments be assigned as security? For example, can payments from your main customers be directed through an escrow or collection account controlled by the lender?

checks.question: Is the proposed security package consistent with the transaction's risk profile?
checks.assumption: Security package adequately mitigates the identified risks
checks.ask: Considering the overall risk profile of the transaction, is the proposed combination of security (collateral, guarantees, assignments) sufficient? Does the total security cover provide adequate protection relative to the loan amount?

checks.question: What exposure does this relationship carry for the facility?
checks.why: Facility exposure drives subject materiality and ask depth

checks.question: What is the maximum guaranteed amount under this relationship?
checks.why: Guarantee cap drives sponsor materiality and ask depth

checks.question: What kind of guarantee does this relationship represent?
checks.why: Guarantee type determines how credit support is interpreted

checks.question: Has a term sheet or heads of terms been agreed between the parties?
checks.assumption: Parties have reached preliminary commercial agreement
checks.ask: Has a term sheet or heads of terms been agreed between your company and the lender/investor? This is the preliminary document that sets out the main commercial terms of the transaction. Please share a copy if available.

checks.question: Are the key commercial terms fully documented — including tenor, pricing, and repayment schedule?
checks.assumption: Key commercial terms are complete and unambiguous
checks.ask: Does the term sheet clearly specify the loan tenor (duration), interest rate or pricing, repayment schedule (amortization or bullet), fees, and any other key commercial terms? Are there any terms still under negotiation?

checks.question: Is the proposed structure appropriate for the entity's risk profile?
checks.assumption: Transaction structure matches the entity's risk characteristics
checks.ask: Does the proposed financing structure (loan type, tenor, repayment profile) suit your company's cash flow patterns and risk profile? For example, is the repayment schedule aligned with your revenue cycle?

checks.question: Are there precedent transactions in this market and sector that support the proposed terms?
checks.assumption: Proposed terms are within market norms for comparable transactions
checks.ask: Are you aware of similar financing transactions in your market and sector? How do the proposed terms compare to those precedents — is the pricing, tenor, and structure in line with market practice?

checks.question: Is the proposed facility size appropriate relative to the entity's debt capacity?
checks.assumption: Facility size is within the entity's borrowing capacity
checks.ask: Based on your company's current revenues, cash flows, and existing debt, is the proposed loan amount appropriate? Can the company comfortably service this debt alongside existing obligations?

look_again_when.reason: Reporting perimeter changed — working-capital trends are not comparable across the restructuring

checks.question: What is the cash conversion cycle?
checks.assumption: Working capital cycle is efficient
checks.ask: How many days does it take from paying your suppliers to collecting cash from your customers? If you don't know this number, we can calculate it from your receivables, inventory, and payables figures.

checks.question: Are receivables aging within normal terms?
checks.assumption: Customers are paying on time
checks.ask: Are your customers generally paying within the agreed credit terms? An accounts receivable aging report would be ideal, but you can also tell us your average days sales outstanding (DSO).
checks.if_unknown: Receivables aging data not available

checks.question: Is inventory management documented?
checks.assumption: Inventory is managed with formal policies and controls
checks.ask: Does your company have documented inventory management practices — for example, stock count procedures, reorder policies, or inventory tracking systems? This is mainly relevant if you hold physical stock.

checks.question: Has working capital requirement increased disproportionately to revenue?
checks.assumption: Working capital scales proportionately with business growth
checks.ask: Over the past 2-3 years, has the amount of cash tied up in your day-to-day operations (receivables plus inventory minus payables) grown faster than your revenue? We can check this from your financial statements if you share them.
checks.if_unknown: Multi-year working capital trend data not available

why_it_matters.debt: Weak board governance may signal lack of oversight, increasing operational risk
why_it_matters.equity: Strong board adds strategic value and protects investor interests

matters_more_when.reason: Operating entity — board oversight of management is a key governance check
Equity thesis — board quality directly affects strategic execution
Equity investor — board representation may be a negotiation point

matters_less_when.reason: SPV — typically no real board; governance flows through sponsor and management agreements

checks.question: Does the entity have a board of directors?
checks.assumption: Entity has a governance body providing oversight
checks.ask: Does your company have a formal board of directors? This is a group of individuals appointed to oversee the company's management and strategy. Even a small board of 3 members counts.

checks.question: How many board members does the entity have?
checks.assumption: Board is appropriately sized for the entity
checks.ask: How many members sit on your board of directors? Please include both executive and non-executive directors.

checks.question: Are there independent directors on the board?
checks.assumption: Board provides independent oversight of management
checks.ask: Does your board include any independent directors — that is, directors who are not employees of the company and have no material business relationship with it? If so, how many?

checks.question: Does the board meet at minimum quarterly?
checks.assumption: Board meets frequently enough to provide effective oversight
checks.ask: Does your board of directors meet at least four times per year (quarterly)? Please share board meeting minutes or a schedule if available.

checks.question: Are board minutes documented and retained?
checks.assumption: Board decisions are formally documented and auditable
checks.ask: Does your company keep written minutes of board meetings? We would appreciate seeing a sample set of minutes from a recent meeting (sensitive details can be redacted).

checks.question: Is there an alternative governance structure (e.g., advisory committee)?
checks.assumption: Entity has no governance oversight mechanism at all
checks.ask: If your company does not have a formal board of directors, is there an alternative oversight body such as an advisory committee, partners' meeting, or shareholder council that provides strategic guidance?

checks.question: Does the entity have documented internal control procedures?
checks.assumption: Entity has a functioning internal control framework
checks.ask: Does your company have written procedures for internal controls? These are the rules and processes that ensure financial reporting is accurate, assets are protected, and operations run as intended. Examples include approval limits, payment authorization procedures, and inventory controls.

checks.question: Is there segregation of duties for financial transactions?
checks.assumption: Financial transactions have adequate separation of authorization, execution, and recording
checks.ask: Are the duties for financial transactions split between different people? For example, the person who approves a payment should be different from the person who executes it, and different again from the person who records it in the books. How is this separation handled in your company?

checks.question: Is there an internal audit function?
checks.assumption: Entity has independent verification of its internal controls
checks.ask: Does your company have an internal audit function — either an in-house team or an outsourced firm that periodically reviews your internal controls, processes, and financial records independently of the finance team?

checks.question: Have there been material control failures in the last 3 years?
checks.assumption: Internal controls have been effective without significant breakdowns
checks.ask: In the last three years, has your company experienced any significant breakdowns in internal controls? Examples include unauthorized transactions, fraud, material misstatements in financial reporting, or significant audit findings. Please disclose any incidents even if they have since been resolved.
checks.if_unknown: Control failure history not disclosed or not verifiable from available documents

why_it_matters.debt: Ownership opacity can conceal related-party risk and impair recovery
why_it_matters.equity: Governance quality directly affects value protection and exit certainty

matters_more_when.reason: Equity thesis — ownership/control relationships directly affect governance and value protection
Equity thesis — shareholder rights and protections are critical
Holding company — control-chain complexity drives structural subordination risk
SPV — sponsor identity and control matter for credit assessment

checks.question: Is the party's ownership and control structure clear and documented?
checks.assumption: Party has transparent, documented ownership and control relationships
checks.ask: Is this party's ownership and control structure clearly documented? We need to understand who owns or controls it, in what proportions, and how those parties connect to the transaction. A shareholder register, company registry extract, or ownership chart would be ideal.

checks.question: Are there ultimate beneficial owners identified?
checks.assumption: Ultimate beneficial ownership is known and disclosed
checks.ask: Can you identify the ultimate beneficial owners — the real people who ultimately own or control the company? We need to trace ownership through any holding companies or trusts to the natural persons at the top.
checks.if_unknown: Beneficial ownership chain incomplete or unverifiable

leads_to.reason: Beneficial ownership identified — detailed UBO verification needed

checks.question: Is there a shareholders' agreement?
checks.assumption: Shareholder rights and obligations are formally governed
checks.ask: Is there a shareholders' agreement in place between the owners of the company? This is a contract that defines shareholder rights, obligations, voting procedures, and exit mechanisms. If one exists, we would appreciate a copy.

checks.question: Are there minority shareholder protections?
checks.assumption: Minority shareholders have adequate legal protections
checks.ask: Does the shareholders' agreement or articles of association include protections for minority shareholders? These typically include tag-along rights, anti-dilution provisions, pre-emptive rights, or board representation requirements.
